page: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine belonging to the Dldsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core compute capabilities and memory-bound operations. The server demonstrates strong single-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2141.0 and single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 31.32 GB/sec. However, multi-core scaling and memory subsystem performance are weaker. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and Passmark memory score fall into the lower performance tier, with large-block memory read bandwidth limited to 36.76 GB/sec and write bandwidth to 25.84 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4lds_v6 offers a specialized resource profile that reduces memory overhead costs for workloads that are primarily CPU-bound. By constraining RAM to 8.0 GB while maintaining dedicated high-frequency Intel Xeon cores, it avoids the premium associated with high-memory instances. This makes it a viable option for single-threaded tasks, lightweight web serving, and basic text processing, though it is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or highly parallelized compilation tasks.

Conversely, the instance exhibits lower performance in memory bandwidth and multi-core scaling, making it a cost-efficient choice for CPU-bound, single-threaded tasks rather than memory-intensive applications.
